+// The machinery panel, drawn. One renderer for both pages: the repo page draws it for
+// one member and the fleet page draws the roll-up, and they are the same shapes — which
+// is why this is its own module rather than two copies that drift.
+//
+// WHAT IT DRAWS, AND WHAT IT REFUSES TO.
+//
+// Every figure is a WINDOW AGAINST THE WINDOW BEFORE IT, because a cumulative total is
+// a number a person reads as a report card and nothing measures. `windowFigure` is the
+// page's own primitive for that and spells the previous figure out beside the arrow.
+//
+// A MISSING KEY IS *NOT RECORDED*. The derivation already answers null for a counter no
+// day had an opinion on; `fmt` below renders that as an em dash and the note beside the
+// tile says which source did not answer. Nothing here coerces a null to zero, and the
+// one place a zero appears is where the window WAS folded and the word did not occur.
+//
+// ONE SCALE PER CHART. Two measures of different magnitudes get two charts, never two
+// y-axes on one — so runs and closes are drawn separately rather than superimposed.
+//
+// PARKS AND LATENCIES ARE TABLES, not charts. The park kinds carry severity, and the
+// page's status palette is reserved for severity; painting four park kinds as four
+// categorical series would spend it on identity. A ruled table says the same thing and
+// is also the table view the contrast rule obliges for the lighter series colours.
+
+import {
+  el, chartLegend, stackedColumns, windowFigure, emptyRow, OUTCOME_COLOR,
+} from './ui.mjs';
+import { detailTable, expander } from './sheet.mjs';
+import { OUTCOMES, PARKS, LATENCIES, change } from '../derive/tasks-machine.mjs';
+
+// A figure, or the em dash that means nobody recorded it. Never a zero standing in for
+// an unknown — the distinction this whole panel exists to keep.
+export const fmt = (n) => (typeof n === 'number' ? n.toLocaleString() : '—');
+
+// Minutes as a person reads them. Under an hour stays minutes, because the latencies
+// this panel reports are mostly single-digit and "0.1h" says less than "6m".
+export const mins = (n) => {
+  if (typeof n !== 'number') return '—';
+  if (n < 60) return `${Math.round(n)}m`;
+  if (n < 1440) return `${Math.round(n / 6) / 10}h`;
+  return `${Math.round(n / 144) / 10}d`;
+};
+
+const money = (n, rate) => (typeof n === 'number' && typeof rate === 'number'
+  ? `$${(n).toFixed(2)}`
+  : null);
+
+// The outcome words, in the colours the rest of the page already gives them. Colour
+// follows the entity: `done` is the same green in this chart as in the queue panel
+// above it, so the two read as one vocabulary and not two.
+const OUTCOME_SERIES = [
+  { label: 'done', color: OUTCOME_COLOR.done, value: (d) => d.done },
+  { label: 'delivered', color: OUTCOME_COLOR.delivered, value: (d) => d.delivered },
+  { label: 'obsolete', color: OUTCOME_COLOR.obsolete, value: (d) => d.obsolete },
+  { label: 'no outcome', color: OUTCOME_COLOR.none, value: (d) => d.none },
+];
+
+const RUN_SERIES = [{ label: 'workflow runs', color: 'var(--s-blue)', value: (d) => d.runs }];
+
+// The sentence every panel opens with: which two spans are being compared, and how much
+// of them the file actually carried. A rate with an unstated denominator is the figure
+// this panel exists not to print.
+export function windowNote(m) {
+  const span = `${m.from} → ${m.to}`;
+  const before = `${m.previousFrom} → ${m.previousTo}`;
+  const folded = m.foldedDays
+    ? ` · ${m.foldedDays.current}/${m.span} day(s) folded this window, ${m.foldedDays.previous}/${m.span} before`
+    : '';
+  return `${span}, against ${before}${folded}`;
+}
+
+// --- the repo panel --------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+export function machinePanel(m) {
+  if (!m.folded) {
+    return [el('div', { className: 'chart-card' }, [
+      el('div', { className: 'k', textContent: 'this repo folds no machinery usage file' }),
+      el('p', {
+        className: 'sub',
+        textContent: 'Everything in this panel comes from `.claudinite/local/tasks-usage.GENERATED.json`, '
+          + 'which the claudinite-tasks pack\'s tasks-usage-fold task writes. Declare that pack and the '
+          + 'panel fills in from its first run; nothing else on this page depends on it.',
+      }),
+    ])];
+  }
+
+  return [
+    reliabilityCard(m),
+    latencyCard(m.latency, m.span),
+    costCard(m),
+    taskCard(m),
+    gapsCard(m),
+  ];
+}
+
+function reliabilityCard(m) {
+  const { current, previous } = m.reliability;
+  const tile = (value, label, prev, note, better) =>
+    windowFigure(fmt(value), label, change(value, prev), note, { better });
+
+  return el('div', { className: 'chart-card wide' }, [
+    el('div', { className: 'k', textContent: 'reliability — what the queue closed, and what it left for a person' }),
+    el('div', { className: 'tiles' }, [
+      tile(current.closed, 'work items closed', previous.closed,
+        current.closed === null ? 'no day in this window is folded' : null, 'up'),
+      tile(current.outcomes.done, 'closed done', previous.outcomes.done, null, 'up'),
+      // More work needing a person is not progress, so the arrow's good direction flips.
+      tile(current.parked, 'parked for a person', previous.parked, null, 'down'),
+      tile(current.parks.failure, 'failure parks', previous.parks.failure,
+        'the only park that holds its task\'s lane', 'down'),
+    ]),
+    chartLegend(OUTCOME_SERIES),
+    stackedColumns(m.days, OUTCOME_SERIES, { detail: dayDetail }),
+    el('div', {
+      className: 'sub',
+      textContent: `${windowNote(m)}. A day the fold has not reached is left blank rather than drawn `
+        + 'at the floor — "not folded" and "nothing closed" are different facts.',
+    }),
+  ]);
+}
+
+// What a day was about, for the hover: the parks it collected, which the column itself
+// has no room for and which is the reader's next question after "how many closed".
+function dayDetail(d) {
+  if (d.source === 'none') return 'not folded yet';
+  const bits = [];
+  if (typeof d.parks === 'number' && d.parks) bits.push(`${d.parks} park(s)`);
+  if (typeof d.runs === 'number') bits.push(`${d.runs} run(s)`);
+  if (typeof d.minutesBilled === 'number') bits.push(`${d.minutesBilled} billed min`);
+  return bits.join(' · ') || null;
+}
+
+function latencyCard(latency, span) {
+  // Quantiles over the window's SAMPLES, taken here rather than read off the file: a
+  // week's p50 is not derivable from its days', which is why the fold carries samples.
+  const rows = LATENCIES.map(({ key, label }) => {
+    const c = latency.current[key];
+    const p = latency.previous[key];
+    return [
+      label,
+      { text: mins(c.p50), gap: c.p50 === null },
+      { text: mins(c.p90), gap: c.p90 === null },
+      { text: mins(c.max), gap: c.max === null },
+      { text: String(c.n), gap: !c.n },
+      { text: mins(p.p50), gap: p.p50 === null },
+    ];
+  });
+  const total = LATENCIES.reduce((n, { key }) => n + latency.current[key].n, 0);
+
+  return el('div', { className: 'chart-card' }, [
+    el('div', { className: 'k', textContent: 'how long each leg took' }),
+    detailTable([
+      { label: 'leg' }, { label: 'p50', num: true }, { label: 'p90', num: true },
+      { label: 'slowest', num: true }, { label: 'samples', num: true }, { label: 'p50 before', num: true },
+    ], rows),
+    el('div', {
+      className: 'sub',
+      textContent: total
+        ? `${total} sample(s) across ${span} days. A leg whose far end never happened — an agentless `
+          + 'item has no hand-off — contributes no sample, which is not a latency of zero. A quantile '
+          + 'is withheld below two samples.'
+        : 'No item closed in this window carried a label timeline the fold could read a latency off.',
+    }),
+  ]);
+}
+
+function costCard(m) {
+  const { current, previous } = m.cost;
+  const spend = money(current.spend, m.minuteRate);
+
+  const workflowRows = m.cost.workflows.map((w) => [
+    w.name,
+    { text: fmt(w.current?.runs), gap: !w.current },
+    { text: fmt(w.current?.jobs), gap: !w.current },
+    { text: fmt(w.current?.minutesBilled), gap: !w.current },
+    { text: fmt(w.previous?.runs), gap: !w.previous },
+  ]);
+
+  return el('div', { className: 'chart-card wide' }, [
+    el('div', { className: 'k', textContent: 'cost — what the scheduler and the executor were billed' }),
+    el('div', { className: 'tiles' }, [
+      windowFigure(fmt(current.runs), 'workflow runs', change(current.runs, previous.runs), null, 'down'),
+      windowFigure(fmt(current.minutesBilled), 'billed minutes', change(current.minutesBilled, previous.minutesBilled),
+        'Actions bills per job, rounded up', 'down'),
+      // Unpriced is the ordinary state — a public repo bills nothing — and the key that
+      // would price it is NAMED, so a reader knows what to set rather than what is broken.
+      spend
+        ? windowFigure(spend, 'spend', null, `at $${m.minuteRate}/min`)
+        : el('div', { className: 'tile' }, [
+          el('div', { className: 'v gap', textContent: '—' }),
+          el('div', { className: 'k', textContent: 'spend' }),
+          el('div', { className: 'sub', textContent: 'not recorded — no actionsMinuteRate in this pack\'s config' }),
+        ]),
+      windowFigure(fmt(current.apiCalls), 'API calls', change(current.apiCalls, previous.apiCalls),
+        current.apiCalls === null ? 'no run in this window printed a cost record' : 'per run, from the cost records', 'down'),
+    ]),
+    // ONE SCALE. Runs get their own chart rather than a second axis on the outcome one:
+    // a busy scheduler superimposed on closed work reads as productivity.
+    //
+    // It is drawn off `runSource`, not the row's own: the run half and the item half are
+    // folded on separate watermarks, so a day carrying items and no run figure is NOT
+    // READ here even though the outcome chart beside it has a real zero for that day.
+    chartLegend(RUN_SERIES),
+    stackedColumns(m.days.map((d) => ({ ...d, source: d.runSource })), RUN_SERIES, { detail: dayDetail }),
+    workflowRows.length
+      ? detailTable([
+        { label: 'workflow' }, { label: 'runs', num: true }, { label: 'jobs', num: true },
+        { label: 'billed min', num: true }, { label: 'runs before', num: true },
+      ], workflowRows)
+      : el('div', { className: 'sub', textContent: 'No workflow run is folded in either window.' }),
+  ]);
+}
+
+// One row per task, both windows on it — so a task that stopped closing anything is a
+// row that went to zero rather than a row that quietly left the table.
+function taskCard(m) {
+  const rows = m.reliability.tasks;
+  const table = el('div', { className: 'detail' }, [
+    detailTable([
+      { label: 'task' },
+      ...OUTCOMES.map((o) => ({ label: o, num: true })),
+      ...PARKS.map((p) => ({ label: `${p} park`, num: true })),
+      { label: 'closed before', num: true },
+    ], rows.map((t) => [
+      t.key,
+      ...OUTCOMES.map((o) => ({ text: fmt(t.current.outcomes[o]), gap: t.current.outcomes[o] === null })),
+      ...PARKS.map((p) => ({ text: fmt(t.current.parks[p]), gap: t.current.parks[p] === null })),
+      { text: fmt(t.previous.closed), gap: t.previous.closed === null },
+    ])),
+  ]);
+  table.hidden = true;
+
+  return el('div', { className: 'chart-card wide' }, [
+    el('div', {
+      className: 'k',
+      textContent: rows.length
+        ? `${rows.length} task(s) produced a closed work item in one of the two windows`
+        : 'no task closed a work item in either window',
+    }),
+    rows.length ? expander('per task', table) : null,
+    rows.length ? table : null,
+  ]);
+}
+
+// The gap note. A number the panel would draw and the file does not carry is STATED,
+// never drawn as an empty series and never as a zero — and the fix is a counter in the
+// fold, which is that task's change to make and not this panel's.
+function gapsCard(m) {
+  return el('div', { className: 'chart-card' }, [
+    el('div', { className: 'k', textContent: 'what this panel cannot show' }),
+    el('ul', { className: 'needs' }, m.unrecorded.map((g) => el('li', { className: 'sub', textContent: g }))),
+    el('div', {
+      className: 'sub',
+      textContent: `Folded through ${m.foldedThrough ?? 'not stated'}`
+        + `${m.generated ? `, last confirmed ${m.generated.slice(0, 16).replace('T', ' ')}Z` : ''}.`,
+    }),
+  ]);
+}
+
+// --- the fleet roll-up ------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+// The same two windows across every member the sweep could read, plus the census of who
+// cannot answer. The census is the denominator every figure above it is read against.
+export function fleetMachinePanel(f, onOpen = null) {
+  if (!f.folding) {
+    return [el('div', { className: 'chart-card' }, [
+      el('div', { className: 'k', textContent: 'no member folds a machinery usage file yet' }),
+      el('p', {
+        className: 'sub',
+        textContent: `${f.readable} readable member(s), none of them folding `
+          + '`.claudinite/local/tasks-usage.GENERATED.json` — everything here waits on the '
+          + 'claudinite-tasks pack\'s tasks-usage-fold task.',
+      }),
+    ])];
+  }
+
+  const { current, previous } = f.cost;
+  const rel = f.reliability;
+
+  return [
+    el('div', { className: 'chart-card wide' }, [
+      el('div', { className: 'k', textContent: 'the fleet\'s machinery, this window against the one before' }),
+      el('div', { className: 'tiles' }, [
+        windowFigure(fmt(current.runs), 'workflow runs', change(current.runs, previous.runs),
+          `in ${f.folding} folding member(s)`, 'down'),
+        windowFigure(fmt(current.minutesBilled), 'billed minutes', change(current.minutesBilled, previous.minutesBilled),
+          f.rates.length ? `priced in ${f.rates.length} member(s)` : 'no member declares a minute rate', 'down'),
+        windowFigure(fmt(rel.current.outcomes.done), 'items closed done',
+          change(rel.current.outcomes.done, rel.previous.outcomes.done), null, 'up'),
+        windowFigure(fmt(rel.current.parks.failure), 'failure parks',
+          change(rel.current.parks.failure, rel.previous.parks.failure),
+          'each one holds its task\'s lane', 'down'),
+      ]),
+      el('div', {
+        className: 'sub',
+        textContent: `${windowNote(f)} · ${f.folding}/${f.readable} member(s) fold this file`
+          + `${f.absent.length ? `; not folding: ${f.absent.map((r) => r.split('/')[1] ?? r).join(', ')}` : ''}. `
+          + 'A member that folds nothing is named here and counted in no figure above.',
+      }),
+    ]),
+    latencyCard(f.latency, f.span),
+    fleetMembers(f, onOpen),
+  ];
+}
+
+function fleetMembers(f, onOpen) {
+  const table = el('table', {});
+  const thead = el('thead', {}, [el('tr', {}, [
+    'member', 'runs', 'billed min', 'closed', 'done', 'parked', 'failure parks', 'API calls',
+  ].map((label, i) => el('th', { className: `cap${i ? ' num' : ''}`, textContent: label })))]);
+  const tbody = el('tbody', {});
+  table.append(thead, tbody);
+
+  for (const { repo, machine } of f.members) {
+    const name = el('td', { className: 'name nw', textContent: repo });
+    if (onOpen) {
+      name.replaceChildren(el('a', { href: `?repo=${repo}`, textContent: repo,
+        onclick: (e) => { e.preventDefault(); onOpen(repo); } }));
+    }
+    const num = (v) => el('td', { className: `num${typeof v === 'number' ? '' : ' gap'}`, textContent: fmt(v) });
+    tbody.append(el('tr', {}, [
+      name,
+      num(machine.cost.current.runs),
+      num(machine.cost.current.minutesBilled),
+      num(machine.reliability.current.closed),
+      num(machine.reliability.current.outcomes.done),
+      num(machine.reliability.current.parked),
+      num(machine.reliability.current.parks.failure),
+      num(machine.cost.current.apiCalls),
+    ]));
+  }
+  // The census, as rows that say so rather than rows of zeroes.
+  for (const repo of f.absent) {
+    tbody.append(el('tr', {}, [
+      el('td', { className: 'name nw dim', textContent: repo }),
+      el('td', { className: 'dim', colSpan: 7, textContent: 'folds no machinery usage file' }),
+    ]));
+  }
+  if (!f.members.length && !f.absent.length) tbody.append(emptyRow(8, 'No member could be read.'));
+
+  return el('div', { className: 'panel scroll' }, [table]);
+}

input.command:
git status --short && git commit -q -F - <<'MSG'
Dashboard: the machinery's reliability and cost panel

Renders `.claudinite/local/tasks-usage.GENERATED.json` — the machinery's own
past-data plane, landed by M1 — on the repo page and as a roll-up on the fleet
page. Nothing reads across to the sessions' `usage.GENERATED.json`: the two are
folded by two tasks on two watermarks, so a member folding one and not the other
is ordinary and the panel says which plane is missing.

`derive/tasks-machine.mjs` is the whole derivation and is pure. Every figure it
returns is a window against the window before it, never a cumulative total. A
counter no day had an opinion on stays null, and the render draws that as *not
recorded* rather than a zero — the two halves of the file answer separately for
that, because a day carrying the item half and not the run half is a real zero
for the outcome chart and NOT READ for the run chart. Latency is carried by the
file as samples and quantiled here, at the window being drawn; the fleet pools
every member's samples rather than averaging their medians.

A member that folds no machinery file is named in the fleet table and counted in
no figure, which is the denominator each number is read against.

Two numbers the panel would draw and the file does not carry — janitor repairs
and leash reclaims — are stated in the panel's own note rather than drawn. No
counter is added to the file here.

Drawn under the dataviz rules: one scale per chart (runs and closes are two
charts, never two y-axes), categorical hues in the page's fixed validated order,
a legend per chart, and park kinds as a ruled table rather than four series
spending the reserved status palette on identity.

# Committing

- **One concern per commit.** If two changes could each stand alone, split them; a message that
  wants numbered items is the split talking.

  else was in progress.

input.title: Dashboard: the machinery's reliability and cost panel (M2)
input.head: claudinite/engine/implement-request/2026-09-15-oxmffm
input.body:
Link **M2** of #1869, implementing #1874. One panel on the repo page and its roll-up on the fleet page, rendered from `tasks-usage.GENERATED.json` alone.

Refs #1869

## What landed

| file | what it is |
|---|---|
| `src/derive/tasks-machine.mjs` | the whole derivation, pure — `tasksMachine` for one member, `fleetTasksMachine` for the roll-up |
| `src/render/machine-view.mjs` | one renderer for both pages, so the two cannot drift |
| `src/views/view-repo.mjs`, `view-fleet.mjs`, `src/index.html` | the two sections and their wiring |
| `test/tasks-machine.test.mjs` (18), `test/machine-view.test.mjs` (8) | the derivation, and both pages rendered from a fixture of the file |

**Reliability** — outcomes this window against the previous (`done`, `delivered`, `obsolete`, `none`), parks by kind, and the four latency legs as quantiles taken *here* over the window's samples (tick→item, item→pick, pick→hand-off, hand-off→converge). **Cost** — runs, jobs, billed minutes, spend where a rate is configured, API calls.

## The rules it renders under

- **A window against the previous window**, never a cumulative total. Every figure is a pair, and the previous figure is spelled out beside the arrow.
- **A missing key reads *not recorded*, never zero.** One `sum` implements it, and the two halves of the file answer *separately*: the run half and the item half are folded on different watermarks, so a day carrying items and no run figure is a real zero for the outcome chart and **not read** for the run chart. Looking at the first render is what caught this — it was drawing a floor line claiming the machinery ran zero times on four days nothing had counted runs for.
- **A member with no tasks usage file is named and counted in nothing** — a census row in the fleet table, which is the denominator every figure above it is read against. It is why nothing in the panel is stated as a rate.
- **No counter added to the file.** Two numbers the panel would draw and the file does not carry — janitor repairs and leash reclaims — are stated in the panel's own note, and the question issue is #2075.

`dataviz` was loaded before drawing. One scale per chart (runs and closes are two charts, never two y-axes); the page's categorical order validated with the skill's own script in both modes (light passes with a contrast WARN on two hues, which the panel's table view relieves; dark passes clean); a legend per chart; park kinds as a ruled table rather than four series spending the reserved status palette on identity.

## Exit, read back on `main`

- whole suite green — **3723/3723**, on this branch rebased onto `ab520dc`
- `check_the_world` exit 0, **zero blocking**; no advisory names either new file
- see-it-fail on both suites: weakening `sum` to return `0` reddened the four unknown-is-not-zero cases; collapsing `runSource` into the row's own flag reddened the two new half-fold cases; flattening the window note and the unpriced tile reddened two render cases

## The screenshot

Delivered to you in the session rather than inline — I have no route to upload an image to a GitHub comment from here. It is reproducible exactly:

```
python3 -m http.server 8099 --bind [REDACTED:env:CLOUDSDK_PROXY_ADDRESS]
```

with a harness page at the repo root importing `/packs/claudinite-dashboard/src/{read/usage,derive/tasks-machine,render/machine-view}.mjs` and this repo's own `.claudinite/local/tasks-usage.GENERATED.json`, clock pinned to `2026-09-15T12:00:00Z`. The harness is scratch and deliberately not in the diff.

Reading off this repo's real file: 52 items closed this window against 61 before, 3 parked, 0 failure parks, 36 runs and 62 billed minutes, spend *not recorded* (no `actionsMinuteRate`), API calls *not recorded* (no run in the window had printed a cost record yet).

## Rebase

Rebased onto `main` past #2068, the tasks pack's `shared-code` → `public` move. Both sides survived: `view-repo.mjs` now imports `../../../claudinite-tasks/public/dormancy.mjs` and my two added imports are intact. Nothing new here reaches into the tasks pack at all.

input.title: Should the tasks usage fold count janitor repairs and leash reclaims?
input.body:
#1874 asks the machinery panel to show "janitor repairs and leash reclaims **where the file records them**". It does not record them, so the panel names both as gaps in its own note (M2's rule: add no counter to the file, state the gap, ask the question here).

The question is whether they are worth a counter, and it is a real question rather than an oversight:

- **A janitor repair** rewrites an item another run left wrong. `tasks-usage.GENERATED.json` folds each closed item's final outcome and parks, so a repaired item is already counted — under the outcome it *ended* at. What the panel cannot say is how many got there by repair, which is the difference between a lane that works and one the janitor is holding up.
- **A leash reclaim** takes an item back from a dead episode. Same shape: the item is folded at its eventual outcome, with nothing saying it needed reclaiming.

Both are readable from an item's own timeline, which `read-items.mjs` already fetches — one read per item closing for the first time — so neither needs a new API call. The cost is two counters and their vocabulary.

Against adding them: the fold's discipline is that every fact is settled once seen and never recomputed, and "was this repaired" is a property of the item's *history* rather than its close, so it has to be read at the same pass or not at all. And a repair count nobody acts on is a number on a page.

No answer is needed for M2 — the panel ships stating the gap either way.

_Filed by the Claudinite task `claudinite-tasks/implement-request`, running as work item missingbulb/Claudinite#1874 — no person asked for this issue._

input.title: session-start.test.mjs reads ambient CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ATTENDED, so it is red in every unattended session
input.body:
`packs/claude-code-web-users-support/test/session-start.test.mjs` takes its answer from the real environment rather than from an injected one. Every queue session exports `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ATTENDED=0`, so the code under test takes its unattended branch and six cases fail:

```
not ok - the store is read locally when this tree IS the store
not ok - a declared path is honoured, not just the default
not ok - no file for this person is a soft note, never a halt
not ok - no usable identity means there is nothing to look up
not ok - the loaded preferences are weighed onto the engine facet channel
not ok - prose weighs the same as bullets — the window does not care about markup
```

with, for the first:

```
The input did not match the regular expression /MY PREFS/. Input:
'USER PREFERENCES: the session is unattended (CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ATTENDED=0) — personal preferences are for a present person; …'
```

`env -u CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ATTENDED node --test <that file>` is green, which is what CI happens to run under, so the suite reads clean there and red in exactly the sessions the queue runs.

The cost is a diagnostic cycle per unattended run: six red cases that look like the session's own change until you work out they are not. The fix is the snapshot rule the repo already holds for clocks — thread the attendedness through the code under test, defaulting to the environment in production and pinned in the test — rather than unsetting the variable at the runner.

Found while running the whole suite for #1874; not fixed there because it is a different pack and outside that item's binding scope.

_Filed by the Claudinite task `claudinite-tasks/implement-request`, running as work item missingbulb/Claudinite#1874 — no person asked for this issue._

input.body:
**M2** (#1874) is delivered in #2076, open for review — no automerge, as the link asked.

Exit, read back on `main` (branch rebased onto `ab520dc`, past #2068's `shared-code` → `public` move):

- the dashboard's tests render the panel from a fixture of the file, on **both** pages — `test/tasks-machine.test.mjs` (18 cases) and `test/machine-view.test.mjs` (8)
- whole suite green, **3723/3723**
- `check_the_world` exit 0, zero blocking; no advisory names either new file
- a screenshot of the rendered panel went to the owner in-session, with the reproduction in the PR body — I have no route to upload an image to a GitHub comment from here

What the panel shows off this repo's own file, for the week to 2026-09-15 against the week before: 52 work items closed (−9), 39 done, 3 parked, 0 failure parks; 36 workflow runs, 62 billed minutes; spend and API calls both *not recorded* — no `actionsMinuteRate` is configured, and no run in the window had printed a `claudinite-run-cost` record yet, which is M1 landing mid-window rather than a gap.

Two things worth carrying forward:

1. The file's **two halves fold on separate watermarks**, and the panel has to respect that per series. Days 09-08 → 09-11 carry the item half and no run figure, and the first render drew them as a floor line — the machinery having run zero times on four days nothing had counted runs for. Looking at the render is what caught it; no test would have.
2. `janitor repairs` and `leash reclaims`, which M2's brief asked for "where the file records them", are **not** in the file. The panel names both as gaps in its own note and the question is #2077 — no counter was added here.

Also filed #2078, unrelated to this plan: the preferences pack's session-start suite reads ambient `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ATTENDED`, so it is red in every unattended session and green in CI.

One panel on the repo page and its roll-up on the fleet page, rendered from `tasks-usage.GENERATED.json` alone, showing per task and per member:

The dashboard's own: a window against the previous window, never a cumulative total; a missing key reads *not recorded*, never zero; a member with no tasks usage file is named and counted in nothing. **Vocabulary:** none new; the panel's words are the file's keys and the queue's existing status and outcome words.

The dashboard's tests render the panel from a fixture of the file (repo page and fleet page); the whole suite green; a screenshot of the rendered panel attached to the PR for the owner.
